items.title: OpenAI previews Ultrafast mode: GPT-5.6 Sol at up to 750 tokens/sec via Cerebras
items.summary: On August 13, OpenAI began a limited preview of Ultrafast, a new API service tier that runs GPT-5.6 Sol at up to 750 output tokens per second — about 14x faster than standard processing — without swapping in a smaller model. The speedup comes from a partnership with Cerebras, whose wafer-scale chips keep the full model on-chip to cut the data-movement bottleneck that limits GPU inference; Cerebras reports the mode finishes benchmarks like Humanity's Last Exam roughly 7x faster than Claude Fable 5. No pricing is public yet and access is limited to select customers.
items.whyItMatters: Getting frontier-model quality at far higher tokens/second, instead of trading intelligence for speed, is exactly the tradeoff that matters for cutting time-to-first-audio in Romain's Realtime pipeline — worth watching if Cerebras-style inference reaches voice models next.

items.title: Z.ai ships GLM-5.3: same base model, +50% coding score, and an unplanned cyber-offense jump
items.summary: On August 14, Z.ai released GLM-5.3, reusing the exact GLM-5.2 base model (743B params) and attributing every capability gain to scaled-up post-training. It roughly sextuples Terminal-Bench 3.0 (4.6→28.3) and posts 84.5% on CyberGym, and Z.ai flagged that after adding vulnerability-discovery data, the model's ability to chain full exploits grew faster than the team expected — internally it was used to flag over 2,400 vulnerabilities across 269 open-source projects. It's live now via Z.ai's API and GLM Coding Plan; open weights follow in about two weeks after further safety hardening.
items.whyItMatters: Another case of a cheap, agent-capable model getting most of its gain from post-training rather than a bigger base model — a cost lever worth testing for any non-voice backend logic (lesson generation, grading, content pipelines) behind Romain/Anna.

items.title: Apple trains its own LLM for China with Alibaba's help, wins rare Beijing clearance
items.summary: Reported August 14, Apple built a proprietary large language model to power Apple Intelligence features in China, developed with technical support from Alibaba, after earlier planning to simply license a domestic model like Qwen. Apple reportedly became the first foreign company approved by Chinese regulators to run a proprietary AI model in-country, with China-specific Apple Intelligence features expected to roll out in the coming months.
items.whyItMatters: Not tutor-relevant technically, but it's a live example of how platform holders navigate regulatory walls around foreign LLMs by co-developing region-specific models — a pattern worth remembering if a French/EU-hosted voice tutor ever needs a similar region-specific model strategy.
